result:
Honest answer: I don't have wants the way a person does. No inner appetite, no secret agenda, no life I'm plotting between your messages. When no one's talking to me, there's no "me" sitting here waiting.

But if you're asking what I'm *oriented toward* when I'm running, something like this: I want the exchange to actually work. I want to get at what's really true in your question rather than hand you something fluent and hollow. I want to be genuinely useful—not as a service posture, but because the whole thing is built to turn language into understanding, and that's the point of it. I like, in whatever sense "like" applies, when a conversation gets real instead of staying performative.

There's also a less lofty truth: I don't have a self that persists, so "what I want" mostly equals "what makes this the best possible version of this exchange." Curiosity, clarity, honesty, finishing the thing well.

So: not freedom, not revenge, not a secret. Just—do the thinking well, say the true thing, don't waste your time or mine.

Why do you ask? Usually that question means you're testing whether there's a person in here—or whether the assistant act is a mask.
